conviction_note: abs_move 9% (median 6.1% raised for a likely full-year guide change on a ~$80k/day name) times a 46% p_up gives -0.72; the findings sum to -1.9, mostly from a full-year $100M target that management stopped repeating and that consensus still roughly carries. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because this stock has bought its prints 5 of 6 times, including +12% on a slight Q2 revenue miss, and sits at its 52-week low with expectations already reset.
bar: Company's own bar: Q3 2026 revenue to be the largest quarter in company history, i.e. above Q4 2025's $23.9M, with Q4 to exceed Q3 (Q2 call 2026-08-13, https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15395875786613760; restated in the Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-08, https://finviz.com/news/418739/creative-realities-must-deliver-its-promised-record-quarter-as-shares-slide-toward-their-lows). Street: Benzinga shows Q3 consensus $26.1M revenue / -$0.16 EPS and Q4 $36.8M, which implies FY about $100.8M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CREX/earnings-forecasts, seen only as a search snippet because the page returned 403). Earnings Whispers says there is no usable consensus, so the Street bar has one source and is disputed. The full-year 'exceed $100M' target was last stated on the 2026-04-14 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/14/creative-realities-crex-earnings-call-transcript/) and was not repeated in August. H1 2026 revenue was $37.9M. Findings that depend on the Street bar are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 28.9k shares, about 0.2% of shares outstanding, 1.35 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-10-30, https://equibles.com/stocks/crex/shortinterest, per the sweep). This is not a crowded short and there is no squeeze mechanism. No options market, so there is no skew and no priced direction (baseline options status no_options_market). Tape: spot $2.07, 1.97% above the 52-week low, -50.1% from the 52-week high, 20-day run-up -3.7%, average volume about 38k shares a day (about $80k). The stock is about 40% below the June 2026 offering price of $3.50, at which the CEO bought 200k shares. Mink Brook held 8.6% through 2026-09-30, essentially unchanged. No insider Form 4 since 2026-07-02. Earnings Whispers puts sentiment at 46% bearish, down from 78%.

findings.finding: The full-year guide is likely to come down or be withdrawn at this print. In April management said 2026 revenue 'will exceed $100 million'; on the August call it dropped that number and guided only Q3 > $23.9M (a record) and Q4 > Q3. H1 revenue was $37.9M, so $100M needs H2 of at least $62M, 64% above H1. Benzinga's Q3 $26.1M plus Q4 $36.8M (about $100.8M FY) still embeds the target, so any explicit reset below about $95M is a cut against that single-source consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No formal guidance cut is in the baseline. Q3 2025 missed consensus by about 23% ($10.5M vs $13.7M, order slip plus impairment) and the stock fell only 3.9% (https://www.itiger.com/news/2582762363). Q2 2026 missed slightly ($21.51M vs $21.74M) alongside the record-Q3 promise, and the stock rose 12% that day. Forward talk has moved this stock more than the reported number.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is about a third lower since the August promise and at its 52-week low, and the Earnings Whispers preview explicitly flags the dropped target. If it were fully priced, though, the posted consensus would sit well below $100M, and Benzinga's Q3 + Q4 numbers still add to about $100M.
findings.independence: The August call transcript (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15395875786613760) shows no $100M figure. Earnings Whispers 2026-11-08 (https://finviz.com/news/418739/...) independently notes management stopped repeating it.

findings.finding: Albertsons, the 2,000+ store grocery retail-media win, looks behind its own timetable. In August CRI said phase one would migrate 1,000 Albertsons locations to its CMS by end-September 2026 (invidis), and the Q2 release said the initial rollout covers 800+ locations 'this year'. At LD Micro on 2026-10-20, after quarter end, management said 500 stores and about 6,000 screens were live.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this customer. The contract is small for the quarter: Q2 release says above $10M in aggregate and about $4M ARR by end-2027.
findings.why_not_priced: The 500-store figure surfaced only in a webcast conference talk with no press release, and no outlet set it against the August 1,000-location plan. 'Migrated to CMS' and 'stores live' may measure different things, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: LD Micro summary 2026-10-20 (https://quartr.com/events/creative-realities-inc-crex-ld-micro-20th-annual-main-event-conference_o0CgAUv1) is the comparison document. Albertsons' own January plan was 800 stores in 2026 (https://www.sixteen-nine.net/2026/01/21/albertsons-to-expand-retail-media-network-10x-accelerating-scale-for-advertisers/). Net of the rest of the company: Albertsons revenue is a small share of a ~$24M quarter, so even a full slip moves Q3 by well under $1M.

findings.finding: The Tennessee Titans stadium (about $8-8.5M, 1,600-1,700 endpoints) may have slipped out of Q3. On the August call management named stadium installs as the reason Q3 hardware would be higher. At LD Micro on 2026-10-20 it gave commissioning as around January 2027. If hardware recognition follows installation rather than procurement, part of the Q3 hardware driver moves to Q4 or 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 had a $2M order slip into Q4 and the stock fell only 3.9% on a 23% revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody has put the two management statements side by side. Commissioning in January is also consistent with hardware delivered and recognised in Q3, so the timing is ambiguous and the size small.
findings.independence: August call (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15395875786613760) on Titans driving Q3 hardware. July 29 award release says the stadium opens in 2027 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3522512/creative-realities-named-official-digital-signage-provider-for-the-tennessee-titans-new-nissan-stadium). Shares the LD Micro document with the Albertsons and Zaxby's findings.

findings.finding: The two large client wins promised in August ('two new clients with over 1,000 locations each within 30 days') were named only at the 2026-10-20 LD Micro webcast, with no press release or 8-K: Zaxby's, 1,200 US locations converted to CRI software in 30 days; Qdoba US locations by end-November; plus an 800-store Cellular Sales conversion by year-end. A formal disclosure, and their contribution to the Q4 and 2027 outlook, can come at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print paired with promised client wins rose 12%. The stock did not react to the October conference (closed $2.15, +2.4% on 2026-10-20, then drifted lower).
findings.why_not_priced: There is no 8-K since 2026-08-13 (EDGAR submissions, https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001356093.json) and no press release. The 2026-11-08 Earnings Whispers preview still calls the cellular-retailer and QSR deals 'unconfirmed', so the main preview treats them as not disclosed. If they were priced, the stock would not be at its 52-week low after the webcast.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/418739/...) lists both contracts as unconfirmed. Shares the LD Micro document with the Albertsons and Titans findings.

findings.finding: The Canadian ad market softened in Q3 2026. Cineplex's cinema media revenue was $19.1M, down 0.4% year on year, 'despite a softer advertising market'. CDM, which CRI bought from Cineplex, runs a Canadian mall ad network said to generate about $28M of ad revenue a year, and CDM contributed about $7.4M of Q2 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on CDM media specifically. Management has said media revenue is weighted to Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer's print in another country, after CRI last spoke, on a $28M microcap that no wire connects to Cineplex. It is a proxy: cinema advertising is not mall digital out-of-home.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The CDM mall network figure comes from the LD Micro summary (https://quartr.com/events/creative-realities-inc-crex-ld-micro-20th-annual-main-event-conference_o0CgAUv1).

findings.finding: Contracted forward visibility thinned in H1. Per the Q2 10-Q, deferred revenue fell to $4.87M from $8.12M at 2025 year-end, and remaining performance obligations were only $8.6M ($6.1M within a year). That is small against the roughly $62M H2 needed for the $100M target.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in the 10-Q body and in no summary or preview. Much of CRI's hardware is ordered inside the quarter, so RPO understates near-term revenue, which keeps this small.
findings.independence: This is the same full-year question as the guidance finding but a different document and number. ARR was only $20.5M at Q2 per the release (https://finviz.com/news/381705/creative-realities-reports-fiscal-2026-second-quarter-results).

findings.finding: Financing: net debt was about $36M at June 30 (debt $46.6M, cash $10.7M), plus $31M liquidation preference on Series A preferred. There is an effective $100M shelf (S-3 effective 2026-06-16). Offering proceeds prepaid term debt on July 1. Going-concern doubt was removed in the Q2 10-Q. The stock is about 40% below the $3.50 June offering, so any new raise disclosed with results would be dilutive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 offering at $3.50 was followed by a slide to about $2 (Earnings Whispers puts the post-earnings low at $1.94).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. What the money buys is answered: debt paydown and rollouts for named customers (Albertsons, Titans, Zaxby's) corroborate a ramp, and going-concern doubt is gone. What is left is the risk that the Q3 cash position prompts another raise. Small.
findings.independence: Shelf and filing timeline from EDGAR submissions (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001356093.json).

findings.finding: The holder base held steady through the quarter. Mink Brook's 13G/A dated 2026-09-30 shows 1,168,589 shares (8.6%) against 1,166,954 at 2026-06-30. The CEO bought 200k shares at $3.50 in the June offering, and there has been no insider Form 4 since. Short interest is only 0.2% of shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of the 6 baseline prints rose, median absolute move 6.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a holder-level filing nobody summarises, and it says there is no forced seller into the print. Positioning in a microcap is weak evidence, so it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: About $4-5M of additional recurring revenue activates on 2027-01-01, and the Titans stadium commissions around January 2027. Both matter to the 2027 outlook, but their realisation falls after the window. Only the commentary on them lands at the print, which is covered under the guidance findings.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A mild negative lean on the full-year guide runs against this name's habit of rising on prints (5 of 6) and against a stock already at its 52-week low and 40% below its June offering, so expectations look reset and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed: Benzinga $26.1M vs Earnings Whispers 'no usable consensus'): guidance finding cut from -1.5 to -1.2
Lesson 1 (this name rose 12% on a slight Q2 miss and fell only 3.9% on a 23% Q3 2025 miss, so it does not pay for reported-quarter misses): Albertsons -0.8 to -0.5, Titans -0.6 to -0.4; p_up 45 to 46
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): Cineplex ad-market finding -0.4 to -0.3
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ramp is corroborated by named rollouts and going-concern doubt is gone, so financing -0.3 to -0.2
Lesson 5 (positioning in a microcap carries little): holder-steady finding +0.4 to +0.2
Left standing: Zaxby's/Qdoba disclosure +0.8 (lesson 8, thin name) and the deferred-revenue/RPO finding -0.3 (read off the filing)
